title: 4 AI Stocks to Buy After NVIDIA's $1 Trillion Comeback
creator: Couch Investor
source_note: Collaboration with The Motley Fool (Neil co-hosts). Detailed summary generated from video captions; auto-captions garble names ('Jensen Wong', 'Lee Bhutan' for Lip-Bu Tan, 'Nebus' for Nebius, 'Core Reef' for CoreWeave).
summary: Couch Investor and Motley Fool's Neil react to Nvidia's board reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO, which added about $1 trillion in market cap in a day, but stress most AI names are still 30-50% off their 52-week highs, so one green day does not prove a turn. Their case is that valuations were already attractive before the drama, the growth story never changed across earnings reports, and no big customer has pulled AI data-centre demand - delays have been permits and construction, not demand. Despite the '4 stocks' title they cover five picks. Intel (INTC, BUY first tracked): consumer CPUs are weak with PCs expensive on memory pricing, about 50% of revenue, and the server-CPU supply chain is unready, but CEO Lip-Bu Tan owns the mistake and server-CPU plus foundry growth should return in 2-3 quarters. Micron (MU, BUY at ~$700, fair value $1,000): about 4x forward earnings, ~75% sold out for 2027, FY26 free cash flow of $50-56B - more than the last 10 years combined. Applied Materials (AMAT, BUY first tracked): wafer-fab equipment growth above 30% in 2027 and advanced packaging up over 90%, where Applied leads. Nebius (NBIS, BUY): still expected to 4x revenue in 2027, funding needs far smaller than a year ago, and Jensen's return should ease funding further. CoreWeave (CRWV, BUY): $130B+ backlog, margins beating expectations, no delays - the business 'just got substantially less expensive' while the growth story did not change.

calls.video_title: 4 AI Stocks to Buy After NVIDIA's $1 Trillion Comeback
calls.thesis: BUY first tracked (collab with The Motley Fool's Neil). Intel is being punished for the right reasons — consumer CPUs ~50% of revenue are weak as memory pricing makes PCs pricier, and the server-CPU supply chain isn't ready for the demand — but CEO Lip-Bu Tan owns the mistake and is fixing it; server-CPU and foundry growth should return in 2-3 quarters, with external foundry customers arriving in H2 next year. Neil: 'more upside than risk from here on out.'
calls.base_case: Supply chain gets fixed and server-CPU/foundry revenue growth resumes over the next 2-3 quarters.
calls.bull_case: Guidance growth returns as the supply chain is fixed and external foundry demand grows.
calls.bear_case: Consumer PC weakness lasts longer and the supply chain stays unready, delaying the recovery.

Applied Materials is his second pick: wafer-fab equipment market growth expected above 30% in 2027 and continuing into 2028, with advanced packaging — one of the cycle's biggest constraints — expected to grow north of 90% next year; Applied leads in that step of the process.
